title: Cabin Floor Seat Track — Bolted Doubler Repair for Localised Corrosion at a Fitting Slot

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Bolted doubler repair for localised corrosion at a seat track fitting slot, used where the pitting is inside the depth limit and a full splice would take the run past its permitted number of splices.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static and fatigue capability of a cabin floor seat track after localised corrosion at a fitting slot has been cleaned up, without cutting out and splicing the section.
sections.damage_assessment: Clean the track over the full length of the affected run and remove the sealant from the fastener line. Map the pitting depth on a 10 millimetre grid with an ultrasonic thickness gauge and record the deepest reading. Corrosion inside the blend limit does not need this repair and may be left blended. Damage deeper than the limit, damage that reaches the lower flange, or damage that crosses a floor beam crossing is outside the scope of this repair and requires an engineering assessment. Record the station of every existing splice and every previous repair in the run before you decide, because the number of repairs a run may carry is limited and a run at the limit must be replaced.
sections.repair_procedure: Blend out the corrosion to a smooth depression with a minimum radius of 10 millimetres and confirm by dye penetrant that no indication remains. Machine the doubler seat so that the doubler sits flush with the track upper surface and does not stand proud into the fitting travel. Prepare the faying surfaces and apply the chromate-free protection to all bare material. Fit the doubler dry and check it with a feeler gauge over its whole footprint; a gap larger than the value on repair drawing RD-53-50-12-909 must be shimmed and not pulled out with the fasteners. Install the clip D5350122405771 at each floor beam crossing within the repair length and renew the upper clip D5350121750926. Install the fasteners wet with sealant, working from the centre of the doubler outwards, using the clevis pins LN666073-13 at the two end positions. Seal the fastener line and the doubler edge. Check that a seat fitting locks and releases at every position across the repair and at one position each side of it.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 20000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a detailed visual inspection of the doubler edge and the fastener line every 6000 flight cycles, and a dye penetrant inspection of the blended area at every cabin refresh. Any new corrosion inside the repair boundary, or any seat fitting that does not lock repeatably, makes the repair invalid and requires the run to be spliced or replaced. Report the repair to Aeralis with the thickness map so that it is recorded against the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Pitting up to 12 per cent of the nominal track thickness over an area not larger than 150 by 40 millimetres, not reaching the lower flange and not crossing a floor beam crossing. One repair per bay and not more than three repairs in any one run.
